ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Don't Let Anger Be Your Boss

fullPassage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life.

As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are. All of these factors can contribute to feelings of anger.

Getting to Know Your Anger

Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.

Questions to Ask Yourself

When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. Why am I feeling this way? Is my anger justified? Am I overreacting? What is the best way to handle this situation? Is there another way to look at this? What would I tell a friend in the same situation? These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act.

First Aid to Calm Yourself Down

When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to calm yourself down. Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a calm state.

Finding Proper Coping Skills

Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.

Conclusion

Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.

questions.passage:
Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool.

(A) The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.

(B) It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly.

(C) When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions. Why am I feeling this way? Is my anger justified?
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 분노는 유용한 도구 → (B) 뭔가 잘못되었을 때 알려줌 → (A) 생산적으로 관리 → (C) 화날 때 자문.
det.analysis:
✅ (B)-(A)-(C): (B) It=anger, 유용한 도구의 구체적 설명 → (A) 핵심은 관리 → (C) 새 섹션
❌ (A)-(B)-(C): It의 지칭 대상이 모호
❌ (C)-(A)-(B): 질문이 먼저 나올 수 없음
❌ (C)-(B)-(A): 순서 뒤바뀜
det.tip: It(B)이 anger(주어진 글)를 직접 가리키므로 (B)가 먼저. 지시어 추적이 핵심.

det.korean: 신체 반응 구체 사례 → 싸움 준비 신호 → 응급처치 방법 순서.
det.analysis:
✅ (C)-(A)-(B): (C) 심박수↑, 얼굴 상기, 주먹 → (A) These=신체 반응, 싸움 신호 → (B) 구체 응급처치
❌ (A)-(B)-(C): These의 지칭 대상 없음
❌ (A)-(C)-(B): 순서 뒤바뀜
❌ (B)-(A)-(C): 구체 방법이 먼저 나올 수 없음
det.tip: These(A)는 (C)의 신체 반응들을 가리킨다. 지시어 추적 + 구체→추상 순서.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. ( ① ) You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. ( ② ) At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. ( ③ ) The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more intense than they really are."

det.korean: '게다가(On top of that)' 호르몬이 감정을 더 강렬하게 느끼게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④: On top of that(게다가)는 뇌 미발달 + 감정 영역 활발에 호르몬을 추가. All of these factors에 호르몬 포함.
❌ ①②③: 호르몬 언급은 뇌와 감정 영역 설명 이후에 나와야 자연스럽다.
det.tip: On top of that = 게다가. 앞의 요인들에 호르몬을 추가로 언급하는 위치.

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. ( ① ) Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. ( ② ) Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. ( ③ ) Another useful skill is problem-solving. ( ④ ) Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful."

det.korean: 신뢰하는 사람에게 이야기하는 것도 매우 도움이 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 대처법 나열 — 산책 → 그림/글쓰기 → 대화(also) → 문제해결(Another)
❌ ①: 방법 나열 시작 전
❌ ②: 첫 번째와 두 번째 방법 사이
❌ ④: problem-solving 설명 위치
det.tip: also(또한)는 앞의 방법들에 추가. Another는 새 스킬 전환.

questions.passage: Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 바르게 배열한 것은?

Don't / let / anger / be / your / boss
ch: Don't let anger be your boss
Don't anger let be your boss
Don't let be anger your boss
Don't be let anger your boss

det.korean: 분노가 당신의 보스가 되게 하지 마라. 사역동사 let의 부정 명령문.
det.analysis:
✅ ①: Don't let(부정 명령) + anger(목적어) + be(원형부정사) + your boss(보어)
❌ ②: 어순 오류 — anger는 let의 목적어
❌ ③: 목적어 위치 오류
❌ ④: be와 let 위치 오류
det.tip: let + 목적어 + 동사원형: 사역동사 구문. Don't let anger be = 분노가 ~이 되게 하지 마라.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 바르게 배열한 것은?

These / are / signs / that / your body / is / preparing / for a fight
ch: These signs are that your body is preparing for a fight
These are that signs your body is preparing for a fight
These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight
These that are signs your body is preparing for a fight

det.korean: 이것들은 몸이 싸움에 대비하고 있다는 신호이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: These are signs(이것들은 신호) + that절(동격: ~라는) + your body is preparing
❌ ①: signs가 주격보어 위치에 없음
❌ ②: that 위치 오류
❌ ④: that이 These 뒤에 올 수 없음
det.tip: These are signs that ~: '이것들은 ~라는 신호이다'. that은 동격 접속사.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become independent. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more active than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions __________ more intense than they really are.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형. 호르몬이 감정을 더 강렬하게 '느끼게' 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① feel(동사원형): make + 목적어(your emotions) + 동사원형(feel)
❌ ② to feel: make는 to부정사를 취하지 않음
❌ ③ feeling: 현재분사, make 구문에 부적절
❌ ④ felt: 과거분사, make 구문에 부적절
det.tip: 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 동사원형! 수동태에서는 be made to do.

questions.passage: These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act. When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes ①<u>flushing</u>, and you may find yourself ②<u>clenching</u> your fists. These simple actions can help ③<u>bring</u> your body back to a ④<u>calm</u> state.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: ① flushing → flushed: become + 형용사(보어). flushed는 '상기된'이라는 형용사.
det.analysis:
✅ ① flushing → flushed: become은 2형식 동사, 보어로 형용사 flushed가 적절
❌ ② clenching: find + 목적어 + 현재분사 정상
❌ ③ bring: help + 동사원형 정상
❌ ④ calm: 형용사, state를 수식 정상
det.tip: become + 형용사(보어): flushed(상기된) vs flushing(현재분사). become 뒤에는 상태 형용사가 온다.

questions.passage: Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of __________ on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사가 와야 한다. instead of focusing on ~
det.analysis:
✅ ③ focusing(동명사): 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(-ing)
❌ ① focus: 동사원형, 전치사 뒤 불가
❌ ② focused: 과거분사, 전치사 뒤 부적절
❌ ④ to focus: to부정사, 전치사 뒤 불가
det.tip: 전치사(of) + 동명사(-ing). instead of + 동명사 구문.

questions.passage: As a teenager, you are going through a lot of changes. You are developing your identity and trying to become ①<u>independent</u>. At the same time, your brain is still growing and is not yet fully developed. The part of your brain that controls emotions is more ②<u>passive</u> than the part that controls rational thinking. On top of that, hormones can make your emotions feel more ③<u>intense</u> than they really are. All of these factors can ④<u>contribute</u> to feelings of anger.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 more active(활동적인)인데, passive(수동적인)로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① independent: 독립적인, 원문 일치
❌ ② passive(수동적인) → active(활동적인): 반의어로 교체
✅ ③ intense: 강렬한, 원문 일치
✅ ④ contribute: 기여하다, 원문 일치
det.tip: active(활동적인) ↔ passive(수동적인). 감정 영역이 이성 영역보다 더 활발하다.

questions.passage: Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you ①<u>trust</u>, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on ②<u>ignoring</u> a solution to the problem that caused your anger. By understanding your anger and finding proper coping skills, you can take ③<u>control</u> of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a ④<u>healthier</u> way.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② 원문은 focus on finding(찾는 데)인데, ignoring(무시하는)으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① trust: 신뢰하다, 원문 일치
❌ ② ignoring(무시하는) → finding(찾는): 반의어로 교체
✅ ③ control: 통제, 원문 일치
✅ ④ healthier: 더 건강한, 원문 일치
det.tip: finding(찾는) ↔ ignoring(무시하는). problem-solving은 해결책을 찾는 것이다.

questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 감정들은 단순히 일상적 삶(everyday life)의 스트레스에서만 오는 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ everyday life: 원문 일치
❌ ① school exams: 학교 시험, 원문에 없음
❌ ② social media: 소셜 미디어, 원문에 없음
❌ ④ family issues: 가족 문제, 원문에 없음
det.tip: everyday life(일상 생활) — 청소년 분노의 원인이 단순한 일상 스트레스가 아님을 강조.

questions.passage: Anger is a natural emotion, and it is not always a bad thing. In fact, anger can be a useful tool. It can tell you when something is wrong or when you are being treated unfairly. The key is to learn how to __________ your anger in a productive way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 분노를 생산적으로 '관리(manage)'하는 것이 핵심이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② manage: 원문 일치 — 분노를 없애거나 억누르는 것이 아니라 관리
❌ ① ignore: 무시하다, 부적절
❌ ③ eliminate: 제거하다, 문맥 반대
❌ ④ suppress: 억누르다, 부적절
det.tip: manage(관리하다) — 분노를 없애는 것이 아니라 생산적으로 관리하는 것이 핵심.

questions.passage: When anger hits, your body reacts physically. Your heart rate increases, your face becomes flushed, and you may find yourself clenching your fists. These are signs that your body is preparing for a fight. But fighting is rarely the answer. Instead, try some first aid techniques to calm yourself down. Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly. Walk away from the situation for a few minutes. Drink a glass of cold water. These simple actions can help bring your body back to a calm state.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 분노를 느끼면 상황에 더 가까이 가야 한다.
깊은 호흡과 10까지 세기는 진정에 도움이 된다.

det.korean: 깊은 호흡(Take deep breaths)과 10까지 세기(Count to ten slowly)는 진정 방법이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 원문 일치: Take deep breaths. Count to ten slowly.
❌ ① increases(증가) ≠ 감소
❌ ② rarely(거의 ~않다) ≠ 항상
❌ ③ Walk away from(벗어나라) ≠ 가까이
det.tip: 원문의 핵심 반전 어구 주의: rarely, away from.

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful. Another useful skill is problem-solving. Instead of focusing on how angry you feel, try to focus on finding a solution to the problem that caused your anger.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 진정된 후 분노를 다루는 건강한 방법을 찾는 것이 중요하다.
일기 쓰기나 그림 그리기로 감정을 표현할 수 있다.
모르는 사람에게 이야기하는 것이 도움이 된다.
분노의 원인이 된 문제의 해결책을 찾는 데 집중해야 한다.

det.korean: 원문은 someone you trust(신뢰하는 사람)이지, '모르는 사람'이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ '모르는 사람'이 아닌 '신뢰하는 사람(someone you trust)'
❌ ① 원문 일치: find healthy ways
❌ ② 원문 일치: drawing or writing in a journal
❌ ④ 원문 일치: finding a solution to the problem
det.tip: someone you trust = 신뢰하는 사람. 친구, 가족, 상담사 등.

questions.passage: Remember, everyone gets angry sometimes. It is a normal part of being human. But you have the power to choose how you respond to your anger. Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your feelings. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions and handle difficult situations in a healthier way.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 분노를 절대로 느끼지 않도록 노력해야 한다.
분노를 이해하고 적절한 대처 기술을 배워 감정을 통제해야 한다.
화가 나면 즉시 감정을 표출하는 것이 가장 좋다.

det.korean: 분노가 보스가 되게 하지 말고, 감정의 보스가 되라는 것이 핵심.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 분노를 이해하고 대처 기술로 감정 통제 — 본문 결론의 핵심
❌ ① 분노를 느끼지 않도록: 원문은 normal part라고 함
❌ ③ 즉시 표출: 원문은 calm down 먼저
❌ ④ 항상 부정적: not always a bad thing
det.tip: 핵심: Don't let anger be your boss → be the boss of your feelings.

questions.passage: Once you have calmed down, it is important to find healthy ways to deal with your anger. ① Some people find it helpful to go for a walk or exercise. ② Others prefer to express their feelings through drawing or writing in a journal. ③ Eating a balanced diet is essential for maintaining good physical health. ④ Talking to someone you trust, like a friend, family member, or counselor, can also be very helpful.
questions.stem: 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

det.korean: ③은 균형 잡힌 식단/신체 건강 이야기로, 분노 대처법과 무관하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 분노의 건강한 대처법을 나열하는 흐름에서 식단/신체 건강은 이탈
❌ ①: 산책/운동 — 대처법 맥락 적절
❌ ②: 그림/글쓰기 — 대처법 맥락 적절
❌ ④: 신뢰하는 사람과 대화 — 대처법 맥락 적절
det.tip: 주제 흐름: 분노 대처법(산책→그림/글쓰기→대화). ③만 신체 건강으로 이탈.

questions.passage: The key is to learn how to manage your anger in a __________ way so that it does not control you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 단어 한 개를 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: 분노를 '생산적인(productive)' 방식으로 관리하는 것이 핵심이다.
det.analysis:
✅ productive: 원문 일치 — manage your anger in a productive way
❌ positive: 유사하지만 원문 불일치
❌ effective: 유사하지만 원문 불일치
det.tip: productive(생산적인) — 분노가 당신을 통제하지 못하게 생산적으로 관리.

questions.passage: When you feel angry, it can be helpful to ask yourself some questions.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

These / questions / can / help / you / step back / and / think / more clearly / before / you / act

→ __________
questions.wa: These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act
accept: These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act
These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act.

det.korean: 이 질문들은 행동 전에 한 발 물러서서 더 명확하게 생각하는 데 도움을 준다.
det.analysis:
✅ These questions can help you step back and think more clearly before you act: 원문 일치
❌ 다른 어순은 문법적으로 부적절
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형: help you step back and think. before + 주어 + 동사.

questions.passage: Don't let anger be your boss. Instead, learn to be the boss of your __________. By understanding your anger, asking the right questions, calming yourself down, and finding proper coping skills, you can take control of your emotions.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어 한 개를 원문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

조건: '감정'이라는 뜻의 명사 1개 (복수형)

det.korean: 분노가 보스가 되지 않도록, 감정(feelings)의 보스가 되어라.
det.analysis:
✅ feelings: 원문 일치 — learn to be the boss of your feelings
❌ emotions: 유사하지만 빈칸 위치의 원문은 feelings
det.tip: feelings(감정들) — 글의 핵심: Don't let anger be your boss → be the boss of your feelings.
